reader_summary: I read the current section as a decision lesson: finishing updates and changing the intended weights demonstrates that training happened, while new-question answers are separate evidence about usefulness. A fixed recipe creates LoRA corrections; validation compares the base and candidates saved after 1,039 and 2,077 updates. Through current 20.6, I understand the correction as trainable A/B maps added to fixed W computation. Through current 20.7 and its freshly rendered figure, I understand that the demonstrated answer and ending supply direct training targets while the question remains readable input: the assistant-boundary position predicts A, and A predicts end. This target-selection step does not itself prove deliverable answer quality. A correction must end normally, retain each required use and strictly beat the agreed combined score. The shown 1,039-update photo results rise from 16/28 to 23/28 and from 31/56 to 53/56, but correct-text chat falls from 4/4 to 2/4 and actual-ASR chat from 3/4 to 2/4. Supplying perfect text bypasses hearing errors, so that first chat decline can expose a problem in answering. Both chat routes have separate no-regression requirements, so photo improvement cannot compensate under this rule. The longer candidate also fails chat retention; each correction has three answers hitting the 384-new-token budget without normal ending. Token is locally defined as a generated text unit that need not be a Chinese character. Neither correction wins the combined-score rule, so the base is retained with the same recognizer. The section explicitly says the base also makes errors and fails to finish some answers, so this fallback is not a promise of full reliability. The chosen weights, data and generation configuration are fixed before final testing, and using final errors to develop the next version requires a new independent final set. These full-experiment results are cited in the prose, not reproduced by my readability work.
